newsitem.title: USA: Consumer spending, incomes up in November.
newsitem.headline: Consumer spending, incomes up in November.

text.p: Consumer spending rose solidly in November as personal incomes rebounded strongly, with big gains in wages and salaries after a flat October, the Commerce Department said Monday.

Spending increased 0.5 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of $5.24 trillion after a revised 0.7 percent jump in October, setting a hearty spending pace for the first two months of the final quarter and suggesting a strong start to the holiday sales season.

Total personal income from all sources, including wages and salaries, rents and interest earnings, increased 0.5 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of $6.57 trillion in November after being flat in October.
Wall Street economists had forecast a smaller increase of 0.3 percent in November spending and a 0.6 percent gain in income.

The department said that private wages and salaries increased $22.5 billion in November after dropping $4.9 billion in October. "In November, employment, average weekly hours and average hourly earnings all increased," it said.

Previously, the department said October personal incomes had risen 0.5 percent. But it revised that upward to a 0.7 percent gain, which department officials said was the strongest monthly increase since a 0.8 percent rise in May.
Gains in personal income are essential for funding consumer purchases, which fuel two-thirds of national economic activity.
Savings were unchanged from October as 5 cents out of each dollar earned was set aside.
Spending on durable goods, which includes cars, furniture and other items intended to last three years or more, rose 0.6 percent in November to an annual rate of $637 billion.
Spending on non-durable products was up 0.2 percent to a rate of $1.56 trillion, while spending for services increased 0.7 percent in November to $3.04 trillion.

The department said that commodity-producing companies boosted their payrolls by $3.6 billion in November after a relatively slight $600 million rise in October. Manufacturing payrolls jumped $3.5 billion following a $300 million October increase.
